description: OFF-BALL: AIM THE DIAGONAL RUN DEEPER, THROUGH THE LINE. One re-aim in the run-target path function of match::player::ActionDiagonalRun (0x144202c20). THIS IS THE AGGRESSIVE PACK OF THE SET - test it last and be ready to revert it. WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES (corrected; the earlier write-up called this a 'clip' and a 'lerp', and it is neither). At 0x144203189-0x1442031b2 the code stores the current run point A into [rdi] and calls 0x144347c20 with xmm2 = 1000.0 (cell 0x145a8dd88), building B = A displaced 1000 units along the run heading. Then 0x1442031c0 `mulss xmm6, C` / 0x1442031d0 `addss xmm6, xmm11` forms the plane X = oppLine + C*attackDir, and 0x1442031d8 calls 0x144349010(&t, &A, &B, xmm3 = X). That callee is NOT a clamp: it computes t = (X - A.x) / (B.x - A.x) with NO clamp, returning false only when |B.x - A.x| <= FLT_EPSILON - which, with B a thousand units out along the ray, effectively never happens. The caller then writes [rdi+4] = A.y + t*(B.y-A.y) and [rdi+8] = A.z + t*(B.z-A.z), and at 0x144203242 `movss [rdi], xmm6` sets target.x = X. It does this on BOTH paths: the al==0 path at 0x144203231 copies A wholesale into [rdi] and still falls into 0x144203242, and xmm6 is untouched on that path. So this is an UNCLAMPED RAY/PLANE PROJECTION: every diagonal run's target is PLACED on the plane x = oppLine + C*attackDir, in x and, because the ray is diagonal, laterally too. Raising C from 5.0 to 8.0 therefore does not merely permit deeper runs - it moves the aim point of EVERY diagonal run 3 m deeper, including runs that today would end in front of the line. THE OFFSIDE COST IS SYSTEMATIC BY CONSTRUCTION, not occasional. HOW BIG IS IT REALLY: smaller than 3 m, because the target is then attenuated toward the player. On the same branch, 0x144203342-0x14420337e computes aim.x = player.x + f2*(target.x - player.x) with f2 = max(ramp*0.6, min(xmm12, max(0.4, ratio))), xmm12 = 1.0 (loaded at 0x144202d33 from 0x1478502b8), so f2 lies in [0.4, 1.0] and the REALISED aim moves +1.2 to +3.0 m. WHEN IT RUNS: on the periodic target-recompute tick only. 0x144202f4c `jge 0x14420307a` splits the function on |[rsp+0x40] - [r12+0x54]| >= (int)(0x14533ea80()*0.3 + xmm10), and the taken side immediately latches the tick at 0x14420307a. Between recomputes a second block steers toward the already-stored target, so the lever still governs every run - but 0x1442031c0 is not a per-frame computation. CORRECTION TO THE EARLIER NOTE ON THE SAFETY NET: the brake named there, 0x144202fc7 (4.0 floor / 12.0 ramp / 0.125 / 0.6 at 0x144202fea, 0x144202ff2), is on the FALL-THROUGH half of that split, which ends at 0x144203075 `jmp 0x1442033eb` and never reaches the clip. Do not use it as a guard address. The patched half has its own byte-identical copy at 0x144203302 (4.0) / 0x14420330f (12.0) / 0x144203325 (0.125) / 0x14420332d (0.6), reached 0x144203242 -> 0x14420329e -> 0x1442032e3; that copy is deliberately left untouched and still slows the runner near the line. HONEST RISK TO THE HEADLINE: it is quite possible that what makes runners pull up on the shoulder is that untouched brake (floor 0.4, ramp 4 m -> 12 m, times 0.6) rather than the 5 m target constant, in which case this pack changes the run's HEADING more than whether the runner goes through the line. That is the thing the in-game test has to answer. VALUES: 8.0 is cell 0x145b52fbc. If offside flags are ugly but you still want to try the lever, 6.0 sits at 0x145ab244c (.tls$, 646 refs, writers 0) for a realised +0.4 to +1.0 m; the stronger steps are 10.0 at 0x145a8dd7c and 12.0 at 0x145c0863c. WHAT IS DEMONSTRATED: (b) unambiguous disassembly, traced end to end - the projection, the unconditional store, the attenuation chain and the branch split were each read instruction by instruction. The identification of xmm11 as the OPPONENT's +0x44 team line is also (b): 0x144202eff computes ecx = ebx^1 and 0x144202f13 loads [rax + 5*ecx*4 + 0x44], the same per-team field ActionSelectorDiagonalRun::vf5 scores on at 0x143e03a0d. (c) inferred: game units, and how the shift interacts with the linesman. Nothing in this pack was emulated. WHO: this is the player-side action executor driven by the AI action selector, which runs for the attacking side only and has no human/CPU test (0x143d0346f guard; 0x143d03493 is the sole caller of 0x143d52470), so it affects the human's AI team-mates and the CPU alike. Whether the stick-controlled player is excluded is NOT established. BYTES: byte-identical in the installed exe and the PRISTINE image; same instruction length; destination 0x145b52fbc is .tls$, non-writable, writers=0; NO pool cell is written (0x145a8dd78 is shared by over a thousand referrers). Revert: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/offball-diagonal-behind.json
